perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is a project manager. He feels frustrated and anxious about poor project progress and initially believes his team is unmotivated.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer, friend, and trusted advice source.
- He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. He told Arthur his team seemed unmotivated and that it was affecting progress. He heard Arthur advise him to understand each team member’s individual motivation, have one-on-one conversations, and make people feel valued and understood.
- After that conversation, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He believed Arthur’s advice could help and decided to implement it.
- In a team meeting, Harold proposed one-on-one chats to learn what motivates each team member. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and urged the team to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He told Arthur this and heard Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to set up another round of meetings to uncover those issues.
- In one-on-one meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns. Team Member 1 told him there was tension between a few team members affecting work. Team Member 2 told him they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks to ease pressure, and said their well-being was important.
- Afterward, Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance.
- He announced to the team that there would be regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and Team Member 2 agree that concerns were being addressed.
- Harold told the team their input and well-being were crucial and urged them to work together to make the project a success.

He does not have access to any private thoughts, hidden motives, or unspoken information beyond what he observed, heard, was told, or did himself.
